name: Mossi Kingdoms
native: Mossi kingdoms of the upper Volta

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the Mossi kingdoms, made part of the Upper Volta colony

ledger.x: c. 1050: the Mossi kingdoms of Tenkodogo and Ouagadougou. "Oubri, who ruled from around 1050 to 1090 CE, is often considered the founder of the Ouagadougou dynasty"; Ouédraogo, son of Princess Yennenga, "built Tenkodogo". The page notes the oral traditions date the story "somewhere between the 11th and 15th…
early: Fada N'Gourma is founded by Diaba Lompo, a son of Ouédraogo; no year on the page, 1100 is a bridge.
c. 1170: the northern kingdoms of Yatenga and Rizim are founded. "Under Komdimie (around 1170), dynasty members split off to form the Kingdom of Yatenga and the Kingdom of Rizim."

1896: the Mossi kingdoms end as independent states and become part of the Upper Volta colony ("They made the Mossi Kingdom part of the Upper Volta colony"); the History of Burkina Faso page has resistance ending only with the capture of Ouagadougou in 1901.

wars.name: Mossi raids on Timbuktu and Walata
wars.outcome: "In the 15th century, the Mossi took over Timbuktu and sacked Walata"; historians debate whether the attackers were Yennenga's descendants.

wars.name: Askia Muhammad's jihad against the Mossi
wars.outcome: Askia Mohammad I "waged a holy war against the Mossi kingdoms in 1497"; the Mossi resisted, and after the Saadi conquest of Songhai in 1591 "the Mossi states reestablished their independence".

wars.name: French conquest of the Mossi kingdoms
wars.outcome: France entered in 1896, ignoring the 1894 British treaty of protection; Mossi resistance ended only with the capture of Ouagadougou in 1901 (History of Burkina Faso page).

certainty.note: The pages give no frontiers or areas; the block is built from provinces round the named capitals.
